definition: A semaphore is a counter that threads wait on and signal. Wait decrements the counter, blocking when it would go below zero; signal increments it and wakes a waiter. A counting semaphore allows a fixed number of threads into a section, not only one.
details: A binary semaphore looks like a mutex but has no owner. Any thread may signal it, which is also why it is easier to misuse.
examples: Limiting a pool to ten concurrent users
Signaling that an item has been added to a queue
